title: Estradiol Topical
overview:
Estradiol increases the risk that you will develop endometrial cancer (cancer of the lining of the uterus [womb]).
The longer you use estradiol, the greater the risk that you will develop endometrial cancer.
If you have not had a hysterectomy (surgery to remove the uterus), you should be given another medication called a progestin to take with topical estradiol.
This may decrease your risk of developing endometrial cancer but may increase your risk of developing certain other health problems, including breast cancer.
Before you begin using topical estradiol, tell your doctor if you have or have ever had cancer and if you have abnormal or unusual vaginal bleeding.
Call your doctor immediately if you have abnormal or unusual vaginal bleeding during your treatment with topical estradiol.
Your doctor will watch you closely to help ensure you do not develop endometrial cancer during or after your treatment.
